Management commits to quarter-on-quarter revenue and profit growth but does not provide specific numerical guidance for next quarter or FY26.
Long-term target to reduce non-prioritized business revenue share to zero over the next five years.
Finance cost as percentage of net sales expected to remain range-bound between 3.8% and 4% over the next couple of years.
Working capital days target of 72 days in short term and 60 days in medium term.
Target debt-equity ratio of 0.7x in long-term steady state.
Credit rating improvement target from current A/A1 to Double A to enable commercial paper issuance.
Blended PBT margin improved 30 bps to 4.74% in Q3 FY25; management expects sustained margin expansion across prioritized verticals.
PEB India net margin target of 7-10% (currently 4.5-5%) over next 1-3 years; US PEB margins already higher than Indian peers.
Solar JV expected to be a 5-6% PBT business; minority interest will not consolidate line-by-line but will add to profit via minority interest line.
Capex for current year about 100 crores; profit substantially higher than capex even before Q4 close; Gujarat PEB plant to be initiated next financial year.
Large diameter tubing project is a long gestation capex project; not a near-term growth vector.
Raebareli plant functional in Q3 FY25, contributed 20-25 crores revenue; expected to hit high capacity utilization between Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26.
US Ascent Buildings new greenfield plant planned to come up next year, similar to Raebareli capacity addition.
PEB India order book at 800+ crores; PEB US order book at USD 50 million plus.
PEB India order book Rs 780 Cr; PEB US order book USD 53.1 Mn
Property, Plant and Equipment Mar'25 Rs 833.07 Cr vs Mar'24 Rs 608.33 Cr, up 36.94%
Capital Work In Progress Mar'25 Rs 53.14 Cr vs Mar'24 Rs 217.63 Cr, down 75.58%

Target debt-to-equity of 0.7 over time

Raebareli plant at 50% peak capacity utilization, targeting high utilization in H1 FY26

PEB India order book INR780 crores, PEB US order book $53.1 million
Strong order backlogs in both India and US PEB, no market constraints
Operating margins of prioritized businesses well over 15%, some at 20%
Q4 FY25 PBT margin 5.2%, up 44 bps YoY
Raebareli plant commissioned in 2024 to expand PEB business in North India
Acquired Ascent Buildings LLC in 2020 to expand pre-engineered building segment in USA

Projects healthy double-digit revenue and profitability growth for engineering services in FY26
Targets finance cost as percentage of revenue to return to 3.xx% range in next 2 quarters
Targets working capital days to reduce from 76 to 60 days long-term
Expects Raebareli plant utilization to reach 70% in Q2 and 80% by year-end
Committed to double-digit revenue and profitability growth long-term across 5 prioritized BUs
PBT margin at 4.75% in Q1 due to labor issues, expects improvement in Q2 as mix shifts to higher-margin businesses
India PEB margins 200-300 bps below competitors on PBT basis, working to improve
Raebareli plant commissioned with 20,000 tons/year capacity, INR300 crore revenue potential at 80-85% utilization
PEB India order book near INR855 crores, US PEB at USD54 million, both trending upward with INR200+ crores new orders booked recently
Capital Work in Progress Rs 125.24 Cr as of Sep-25 vs Rs 53.14 Cr Mar-25
Management commits to a floor of 20% PAT growth sustainably over the next few years.
Management targets PBT margin of 7.5% as terminal velocity over the next three years.
Q2 PAT margin was 3.56%, slightly muted due to one-time acquisition costs and labor issues; expected to improve from Q3.
Gross margin impact from labor cost increase of Rs. 500 per ton, potentially reducing operating margin by 30-40 basis points, but offset by scale effects.
PEB India order book stands at Rs. 880 crores, expected to hit Rs. 900 crores by December and cross Rs. 1,000 crores in next few months.
US PEB active order backlog is healthy, currently well above $54 million, with expectation to book $10 million per month going forward.
Boilers and process equipment order backlog rose significantly to Rs. 126 crores, expected to drive robust revenue growth in Q3 and Q4.
Consolidated order book across all divisions is Rs. 956 crores for execution in next 4-6 months, up over 20% year-on-year.
Capacity expansions coming online for Body in White division in coming quarters; PEB capacity utilization expected north of 75% in Q3.
New PEB plant at Raebareli is operational, boosting capacity and future revenue potential
Management guides for double-digit revenue and PAT growth for full year FY26 and double-digit PAT growth north of 20% for FY27
Long-term sustainable PAT margin target of 7% within next 2 to 3 years
Finance cost guidance maintained at 4% of net revenue (1% long-term loans, 3% working capital)
Consolidated tax rate guided at approximately 25.5%
PEB India order backlog at INR810 crores; US combined Ascent Buildings and Ascent Structural order book at $60.6 million ($52M buildings + $10M Telco)
Boilers division order backlog increased to INR123 crores with strong export orders from Australia, Sri Lanka, Saipem, Browns Industry
Hydraulics order backlog more than doubled; US tariff reduction from 50% to 18% to accelerate growth
Q3 PAT margin at 3.56%; excluding one-time costs would have been 4%; revenue and profit trajectory shifting to higher-margin businesses
ROCE at 21.3% and ROE at 12.1%; confident of sustaining returns as performance scales
Depreciation increased by INR4.25 crores (INR1.33 cr standalone from capex and repair/maintenance capitalization; INR2.92 cr subsidiary from Telco acquisition and robotic machines at US operations)
PEB India capacity utilization improved, manpower challenges eased, inventory reduced by ~4,000 tons; Engineering services capacity locked but quickly expanding
PEB India order book at INR810 crores; US Ascent buildings order backlog at USD52 million, structural at USD10 million, combined USD62 million
Hydraulics order backlog projected to more than double in next few weeks due to US duty change from 15% to 18%
Boiler business order book at INR123 crores, expected to be executed within next six months (blended average of 3-4 months for process boilers, 9 months for power boilers)
Peak combined India and US PEB/structural capacity at 80% utilization could generate INR200-220 crores per month
EBITDA margin guidance inclusive of other income; sustainable EBITDA margins growing year-on-year; one-time costs in Q3 (acquisition-related INR1-2 crores, other items) not expected to recur
New express line commissioned in US; Raebareli plant ramping up; further PEB capacity expansion in India under discussion, details next quarter

Management guides finance cost to remain below 4% for the full year

PEB India capacity utilization at 70% in Q4 FY26, targeting around 80% in FY27
PEB India order backlog at INR810 crores, PEB U.S. at $63 million, Boilers at INR145 crores, Hydraulics at INR34 crores
Q4 PAT margin improved to 4.44% from 3.9%; full year PAT margin at 3.83% vs 3.7% in FY25; expects positive trajectory to strengthen through 2027
Gross margins guided to remain at similar 42-43% level

Management targets ROCE of 25% for FY27 and debt-to-equity around 0.7 by year-end.
Management targets PBT margin of 7% over the next 3 years, up from current 5.38%.
Management expects PAT growth of at least 20% for FY27.
PEB India order book at INR1,008 crores, highest ever.
PEB U.S. order backlog crossed USD 100 million, a new peak.
Boilers order backlog at INR150.75 crores, highest ever.
PBT margin improved to 5.38% from 4.77% YoY; gross margin expanded to 43.85% from 42.56%; contribution margin rose to 28.51% from 27.14%.

BIW plant commissioned; expected to double BIW revenue over next three months.
